title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 12
paragraphs: That was all that was said at the time. But later, when darkness came on, the opinion of Artabanus tormented Xerxes, and making the night his counsellor he found that it was by no means to his advantage to march against Greece. Having reached this new resolve, he fell asleep, and during the night he saw, as the Persians report, the following vision: Xerxes dreamed that a tall, handsome man came and stood by him and said: “Are you really changing your mind, O Persian, about leading an expedition against Greece, now that you have proclaimed that the Persians should assemble an army? You do not well to change your mind, nor will the man now here with you excuse you for it. Go by the way you decided upon in the day.”
